_note: Stage G / v4 Tier 6: the trapdoor, the Undercroft, Clementine, S26 and the endings (first bible section 11; addendum K: Clementine mentions Cole). SPOILERS.

trapLocked.title: The trapdoor
trapLocked.text: A cold draught comes up the shaft, and far below a lamp is burning. Danny's voice crackles on your radio. "Not yet, Chief. Whoever lit that lamp, we go down there with the whole case in our hands. Every investigation solved, and the theory filed at the typewriter (S26)."

climbPrompt: Climb back up to the office

standoff.intro: The trapdoor swings up. Iron rungs go down into the dark, and at the bottom, in the light of a lantern, stands Ox with a wrench in his fist.
standoff.ox: Don't come down, Inspector. Please. There's nothing down here.

options.label: I'm not here to hurt anyone, Ox. Step aside.
options.ok: His shoulders drop. He lowers the wrench, slowly.
options.no: "I can't. I promised." He doesn't move.

options.label: One extra ration, every day, for two years. I know, Ox.
options.ok: He closes his eyes. "Then you know already."

options.label: Out of my way, or I'll have you for obstruction.

standoff.voiceWho: A woman's voice, from somewhere beyond the lantern
standoff.oxLeaves: Ox lets out a long breath, squeezes past you up the rungs without a word, and goes back to his shed. The lantern stays lit below.

UC_Tray.name: A tray on the shelf
UC_Tray.text: A tin tray with two cups and a plate, still warm. Somebody brought supper down here not long ago.

UC_Mural.name: The sky
UC_Mural.text: Every inch of the ceiling and walls is painted: a blue sky, soft clouds, and little aeroplanes, dozens of them, all flying the same way. Out.

UC_Drawings.name: Drawings
UC_Drawings.text: Pencil drawings pinned to the concrete: the Trimotor from every angle, the beacon tower, a man's face drawn over and over and crossed out each time.

UC_Calendar.name: Scratches on the wall
UC_Calendar.text: Tally marks in chalk, in fives, hundreds of them. Seven hundred and thirty-three days. The last one is very neat.

UC_SpoonKey.name: A Morse key made from a spoon
UC_SpoonKey.text: A teaspoon handle bent into a sending key, wired to a contact, and the contact spliced into the thick black cable that comes out of the wall. The telegraph line. Whoever sent your telegram sent it from here.

UC_Bed.name: An iron bed
UC_Bed.text: A narrow iron bed, made very neatly. Under the pillow, a pair of soft cotton gloves with the fingertips worn through.

diary.title: Her diary
entries: Day 1. They moved me here from the clinic in the night. I am told I am dead. Papa says it is for my own good. It is very dark and smells of petrol.
Day 9. My hands are still wrapped up like a parcel. The doctor comes at night and does not look at my face.
Day 30. A man brings my food. He is enormous and he is afraid of me. His name is Abel. He says grace over my soup.
Day 61. There is a wire in the wall that sings. Clicks. Long and short. Somebody up there is talking to the sky.
Day 140. I have learned the alphabet of the clicks. The man who sends them stumbles on his Q. I like him.
Day 200. I painted the ceiling blue. Abel brought the paint and pretended he hadn't.
Day 311. Papa came down. He stood at the bottom of the ladder and could not come any further. I said, you could just let me go. He went back up.
Day 402. I found the old pipe that goes under the other building. There are jars there. One of them is the kind of thing you keep for yourself.
Day 405. I took a little of it. For me. For when I decide.
Day 600. I made a key out of a spoon. I can make the wire sing back.
Day 729. I sent a telegram. To an inspector in the newspapers, a man who does not give up. I signed it with Papa's name, because it is my name too.
Day 731. Papa is going to tell everyone. I heard him through the vent. And then I heard the rest: Zürich, at five, asleep. Not free. Further away.
Day 732. I decided who it was for.
Day 733. He is coming. The inspector. I hope he is kind. I hope he is not.

clementine.name: Clementine Pryce
clementine.open: You're later than I hoped, Inspector.
clementine.reply: Yes. The girl who died on the Marigold. Sit down, if you like. Then tell me what you know. Not what you think. What you know.

prompts.q: Everyone says it was his heart.
prompts.right: She lifts her head. "No. It wasn't."

prompts.q: The door was bolted. He was alone.
prompts.right: "Yes. I wound it for him. He used to wind it for me."

prompts.q: Anyone could have touched that decanter.
prompts.right: She looks at her gloved hands and says nothing.

prompts.q: And you think you know who sent for you.
prompts.right: "The man upstairs stumbles on his Q. I copied him. It seemed polite."

prompts.q: I died, Inspector. It was in the papers.
prompts.right: "He got there before anyone. He carried me out himself."

prompts.q: And how would a dead girl get into a locked room?
prompts.right: She glances up, at the trapdoor. "The same way I get everywhere."

clementine.wrong: She turns her face away. "That isn't it."
clementine.notEnough: You don't know. Not really. Come back when you do, Inspector. I'm not going anywhere. That was rather the point.
confession: I kept that poison for myself. Eleven months, in a tin, under the bed. Then I heard him say 'Zürich', and I decided who it was for.

I put it in the decanter that afternoon, from below. At twenty to ten he drank to Marigold, the way he always did. I listened until it was quiet. Then I went up and wound my music box, because I didn't know what else to do.
I didn't send for you to catch me, Inspector. I sent for you to find me. I didn't know yet that I would do the other thing.
He knew the mount was cracked. He knew about the weather. He carried me out of the fire whispering 'don't tell them you were aboard'. Not because he was ashamed. Because I was proof.
You brought a boy with you. The one who talks to himself in the shed. Look after him.
clementine.papers: She slides her diary and a bundle of papers across the floor to you: the 1931 maintenance log, the real weather report, her father's letter.

choices.label: Bring her up into the daylight, and tell everyone everything.

S26.title: The Board and the Theory
S26.intro: At the typewriter: file your theory. Who killed Cornelius Pryce, how, where they came from, and why. Only established findings will stand up.
where: Up through the trapdoor under the rug
Through the door, before it was bolted
why: He was about to send her away to Zürich, sedated, for good
To be free of an unhappy marriage
S26.notEstablished: You can't file that yet: these findings aren't established:
S26.wrongWho: File it anyway? An innocent person may hang for this.
S26.filed: Theory filed. Danny reads it over your shoulder and goes quiet. "Then she's down there, Chief. Under the office. All this time."
S26.wrongFiled: You file it. Danny says nothing at all.

E1.title: The Law
lines: Clementine Pryce climbs the iron rungs at noon with her gloved hands in front of her, and Danny puts the cuffs on gently.
The trial is in Reno in the spring. The papers call her 'the Ghost of Sable Flat'. They print the real weather report, the cracked mount, the insurer's money.
Tamsin Quill, Abel Brennan, Doctor Lindqvist and Julian Ferreira-Blake are all charged in the matter of the Marigold.
Clementine is convicted. On the day of the sentence she asks the judge if she may see the sky first. He says yes.
You keep the music box. Some nights you wind it.

E2.title: The Silence
lines: You rule the death natural causes, heart failure, and sign it in your neatest hand. Danny watches you do it and doesn't say a word.
At dawn the Trimotor takes off into a clean sky with Billie at the controls, Lindqvist in the cabin, and a girl in a veiled hat looking out of the window.
Everyone else drives away free. The Marigold stays a crash and nothing more.
Years later, postcards start arriving from Zürich. No name. Always a little aeroplane drawn in the corner.
You carry it alone. That was always the price of silence.

E3.title: The Daylight
lines: You bring her up the ladder and out through the hangar doors, and for the first time in seven hundred and thirty-three days Clementine Pryce stands in the sun. The storm has gone. She shades her eyes and laughs at the wrong moment.
At the trial her diary is read aloud, and Billie's 1931 photographs are passed along the jury box: the truck at the wreck before the rescuers, the stretcher under the canvas.
The Marigold truth comes out all at once: the order to fly, the false weather, the cracked mount, the buried inquiry. It ruins everyone who kept the silence.
Clementine is acquitted. She learns to fly.
The last postcard you get from her is of an aeroplane over the Alps. On the back: 'Found.'

E4.title: The Wrong Person
lines: You name the wrong person, and the evidence, such as it is, is enough for a jury that wants an answer.
At dusk the storm lifts and the Trimotor leaves with Billie at the controls and a passenger nobody counted.
Under the hangar, a lantern burns out and is not lit again.
Years later you still dream about a music box playing in a locked room.

E5.title: Cold Case
lines: Half past five. The storm clears, the strip is open, and nobody needs your permission to leave.
By nightfall Sable Flat is empty. The case goes cold, and stays cold.
The last thing you see as your plane climbs away is the hangar, a single lamp glowing under the roof vent, and a small silhouette at the window, watching you go.

E1short.title: The Daylight, Too Soon
lines: You bring her up into the daylight before you can prove what was done to her.
Without the photographs and the papers, the trial is about one poisoned decanter and nothing else. The Marigold stays buried.
Clementine Pryce is convicted. The people who made her keep their secrets.
You keep the music box. Some nights you wind it.
